slot.brief: Ask about inversion/retention and racemisation for a chiral substrate under SN1 vs SN2 conditions, or which substrate/conditions lead to racemisation.

stem: Which reaction is expected to give a racemic substitution product at the carbon bearing the leaving group?
options: 2-bromobutane reacting with sodium azide in dimethyl sulfoxide
Optically pure 1-chloro-1-phenylethane undergoing solvolysis in aqueous ethanol
1-bromobutane reacting with sodium cyanide in dimethyl sulfoxide
2-bromobutane reacting with sodium iodide in acetone

verdicts.working: (A) undergoes benzylic SN1 solvolysis via a planar carbocation, so attack from either face gives racemization. (B) and (D) undergo SN2 inversion; (C) has no stereogenic carbon at the substitution site.

working:
$\text{1-chloro-1-phenylethane}$ forms a resonance-stabilised benzylic carbocation during solvolysis. Its planar intermediate can be attacked from either face, giving a nearly racemic substitution product. The other listed substitutions proceed mainly by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ or do not involve a chiral reacting carbon.

Independent check: (A) undergoes benzylic SN1 solvolysis via a planar carbocation, so attack from either face gives racemization. (B) and (D) undergo SN2 inversion; (C) has no stereogenic carbon at the substitution site.
solution:
Solvolysis of optically pure 1-chloro-1-phenylethane forms a resonance-stabilized, planar benzylic carbocation.
$$\text{Ph–CH(Cl)–CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{Ph–C}^+\text{H–CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{attack from either face}} \text{racemic substitution product}$$
Thus, substitution at the chiral carbon gives a nearly racemic product.
